title: Duplicates in a Kafka consumer
context: Kafka gives at-least-once delivery by default, so a consumer can see the same message twice. How do you make a consumer that credits cash to accounts safe against duplicates?
answer: Assume redelivery happens (after crashes, rebalances or a failed offset commit) and make processing idempotent. Give every event a unique id and record processed ids in the same database transaction as the side effect, with a unique constraint; a duplicate then hits the constraint and is skipped. Commit offsets only after processing. Where possible make the operation naturally idempotent, such as setting a state instead of incrementing. If the consumer also publishes events, use a transactional outbox. Kafka's exactly-once transactions only cover Kafka-to-Kafka flows, not writes to your own database.

points.title: Redelivery is normal
points.why: Crashes, rebalances and failed offset commits all cause the same message to be processed again.

points.title: Deduplicate by event id in the same transaction
points.why: Store processed event ids with a unique constraint alongside the credit, so both commit or neither does.

points.title: Commit offsets after processing
points.why: Committing first can lose messages; committing after means duplicates instead, which dedup handles.

points.title: Prefer naturally idempotent operations
points.why: Setting a status or upserting by key is safe to repeat; incrementing a balance is not.

points.title: Exactly-once is Kafka-to-Kafka only
points.why: Kafka transactions don't cover your database writes, and publishing needs an outbox.
